q: The object of inspection of executive offices and field units by Accounts Inspection teams of Divisional and Hqrs. Accounts officer's is

options.A: To ensure that returns/vouchers submitted to Accounts for internal check are correctly prepared based on facts and as per procedure laid down
options.B: To ensure that all initial records are kept and maintained efficiently to produce as reliable evidence in Court of Law

e: Option (D) is correct: Accounts Inspection of executive offices and field units serves both purposes. Inspection is the on-the-spot verification of cash, stores, tickets and records to ensure rules are followed and leakages caught early. Remember: Watch the timeline or sequence in such questions; many errors come from mixing up the order. Make a one-line note of this concept for revision; it recurs in several papers.

q: Statement (A): The inspections of executive offices embrace only test check ofinitial records: Statement (B): It is necessary that during the inspections it is to be verified, whether there are any defects in the procedure followed, either through ignorance, wrong application; deliberately which affect the financial interest of the Railway:
e: The correct answer is Both Statements (A) and (B) are correct. Option (C) is correct: both statements stand. Statement (A) is correct because inspections of executive offices embrace a test check of initial records. Statement (B) is also correct because during inspection it must be verified whether there are defects in the procedure followed — through ignorance, wrong application, or deliberate action — that affect the financial interest of the Railway. Inspections therefore detect both factual errors and procedural defects harmful to railway finance.

The inspection jurisdiction of Accounts is thus comprehensive, spanning both administrative offices and field-level stores custody.

It covers inspection of offices under the accounts control of Headquarters offices, inspection of Unit Accounts offices, Divisional Accounts and Workshop Accounts, and also book stalls, training centres, educational institutes, canteens and all other policy issues relating to working that have financial implications. q: While verifying the imprest cash during the check of executive office is to be verified by actual count and tallied with the book balance, and a certificate is to be recorded to the effect in the register under the initials of inspecting official:
e: Cash on Hand — that is the right answer. Option (A) — "Cash on Hand" — is correct: while verifying imprest cash at a unit office, the inspecting official must verify the cash by actual count, tally it with the book balance, and record a certificate to that effect in the register under his initials. The certification confirms physical cash on hand, not merely vouchers, establishing that the cash actually held agrees with the books.

q: While verifying the imprest cash transactions ofa unit office it is checked to see that is not in excess of requirement and justification exists, and if it is found that recoupments are made occasionally of imprest is suggested indicating the adequacy:
e: Sanctioned Amount Reduction Balance Amount Cancellation — that is the right answer. Option (B) is correct: while checking imprest cash transactions of a unit office, the imprest must not be in excess of requirement, and recoupments should be frequent enough to justify the sanctioned amount. If recoupments are made only occasionally, the imprest is larger than needed, and reduction of the sanctioned amount is suggested — indicating the inadequacy/over-provision of the imprest.
